title: Coaching call — scoring rubric

discrepancies.what: Dimension maxima do not sum to the stated total
discrepancies.computed: the twelve printed maxima sum to 105
discrepancies.resolution: Scored on the printed maxima and normalised: raw / 105 x 100. The printed per-dimension tables are the only numbers the rubric actually supports, and normalising is the method the rubric itself prescribes.

discrepancies.what: Stated total with D4 disabled does not match the printed maxima
discrepancies.resolution: Used 90 as the denominator when D4 is disabled, then normalised to 100 — the same method the rubric prescribes for that case.

dimensions.title: Check-In & Connection
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach open with genuine curiosity and gauge the client's real state before anything else? Does the call intention get set explicitly?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Coach asks about body, wins, AND struggles. Listens before responding — no interruption. Reflects what they hear back to the client ("What I'm hearing is…"). States clear call intention tied to client's actual state. Coach reads what kind of call is needed today and adjusts the approach accordingly.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Good questions but limited depth. Solid check-in, reflects but not fully. Call intention stated but generic ("let's keep making progress on your goals").

buckets.label: Surface
buckets.criteria: Surface-level: "How's it going?" Doesn't reflect. Moves to program topics within 30 seconds. No call intention stated.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Skips check-in entirely or rushes through. No acknowledgment of client's state. Launches directly into program content.

positiveSignals: Coach adjusts call plan based on check-in answers
Client opens up beyond surface level
Intention is stated and tailored to this client's current moment.
negativeSignals: Monosyllabic client response and coach moves on
notes: "The check-in is how you gauge what kind of call this person actually needs today. The framework is a container, not a script. If someone hops on in tears, you put the framework away. Meeting them where they're at IS the framework working."

dimensions.title: Diagnostics Review
dimensions.whatToLookFor: When applicable, does the coach demonstrate expertise through specific, personalized feedback — not generic commentary? Is 1–2 movements reviewed (not more), and are findings tied directly to client goals?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Screen shares 1–2 movements only (per SOP). Makes specific, anatomically precise observations. Directly ties findings to client's stated pain points and goals: "See how your hips shift here? That's why we're building ___." Client clearly understands the connection. Coach selects movements that point back to client's why.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Good observations but not fully tied to goals. Expertise shown, context-linking incomplete. Reviews correct number of movements.

buckets.label: Surface
buckets.criteria: Reviews movements with generic feedback ("Good effort, keep your back straight"). No tie to client goals or pain points. Possibly reviews too many movements.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Skipped, rushed, or unclear. Feedback generic or absent. Personalization not visible.

positiveSignals: Coach explicitly selects movements tied to client's presenting goal
Anatomical specificity
Client has a visible "I didn't know that" moment.
negativeSignals: Generic cues not connected to goals
notes: "One to two movements — not a hundred. Very specific. Always pick the movements that point back to the client's goals, their why."

dimensions.title: Program Focus + Vision
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the coach connect the current block to the client's 12-month vision and identity? Or do they only talk about this week?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Clearly explains what the current block targets (e.g., baseline strength, mobility, metabolic capacity). Explicitly connects this phase to client's 12-month vision by name. Reinforces Halden Method difference: "We build from your diagnostics and goals — not random workouts." Client responds with belief or insight. Client leaves understanding not just WHAT but WHY this specific block, at this specific time, is the path to their specific goal.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Block explained and connected to goals but vision tie is generic ("this builds toward your long-term health"). Emotional resonance present but not sharp.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Vague explanation. Block explained as logistics only. Client understands what to do this week but not why it matters long-term. No 12-month vision referenced.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No explanation of block. Just "keep doing your workouts." No connection to vision.

positiveSignals: 12-month vision referenced by name
Client responds with buy-in or insight
Block tied to previous and next phase.
negativeSignals: Reframe not attempted when client is confused.
notes: "Connect back to: why did they join? What's the progress they've made? And where are they going — not just where, but WHY are they going there? Why is that important?" This is the #1 loss dimension in coaching call QC. Most coaches explain the program but forget to build the belief.
#1 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: "They explain the program but forget to make the client believe in the journey."

dimensions.title: Movement Coaching Quality
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does something actually improve or click during this call? Is the coach coaching — or just narrating?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Reviews 1–2 movements live. Specific cues given: setup, breathing, control. Asks reflective questions: "Where do you feel this most?" / "What felt hardest here?" Improvement is observable or client verbally confirms a new understanding. Links back to goal: "This is what's moving you toward ___." If client is a "talker," coach redirects to live movement.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Clear coaching and relevant cues. Missing reflective questions or goal link. Client engaged but no breakthrough or redirection of talker dynamic.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Mostly telling ("Keep your back straight, squeeze your glutes"). No reflective questions. No back-and-forth coaching exchange.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No live coaching. Just commentary or "looks fine." Client is a passive observer. Coach lets the call become purely talk without movement.

positiveSignals: Client has an "aha" moment
Coach adjusts cue based on client response
Live exchange (back and forth)
Talker redirected to movement.
negativeSignals: Client spends 8 minutes talking and no movement happens
notes: "The best thing for the person who just wants to talk is probably going to be some movement. We all know that person — they love to talk a good game but they don't actually want to do the stuff that's going to get them to their goals." Elite coaches gently insist on live movement even with talkers.
Detection criteria — ALL four must be absent to disable: > 1. Client performed any live movement during the call.
#3 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: "Coaches narrate instead of coaching. Without live exchange, reflective questions, and a goal link, the call becomes commentary — not real coaching."

detectionCriteria: Client performed any live movement during the call.
Coach gave setup, breathing, or control cues in response to a movement.
There was a video review of a recorded movement attempt with real-time feedback.
Coach gave real-time form correction while the client moved.

dimensions.title: Adjustments & Strategy
dimensions.whatToLookFor: When adjustments are made — training or lifestyle — are they framed as intelligent, strategic progress? Or do they feel like a step backward?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Adjustments explained with clear rationale tied to the client's long game. Explicitly framed as protection and strategy: "We're adapting — not backing off. This protects the long game." Both training and lifestyle constraints addressed if applicable. Client leaves feeling smarter and more confident, not discouraged.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Adjustments made and explained. Framing present but brief. Client doesn't feel discouraged but isn't fully empowered.

buckets.label: Surface
buckets.criteria: Adjustments made without clear rationale. Client accepts changes but doesn't understand why. Subtle discouragement possible.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Reactive, unexplained changes. Client confused or mildly demoralized. No protective framing applied.

positiveSignals: Client says "Oh, that makes sense"
Adjustment tied to the bigger goal
Coach explains what the adjustment builds toward.
negativeSignals: "Let's reduce that for now" with no explanation

dimensions.title: Action Steps & Accountability
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Do both the coach AND client leave with specific, time-bound, measurable commitments? Is verbal ownership created — not just instructions given?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Coach states commitments out loud: "I'll the video tool you feedback on ___ by ___." Client commitments are specific: "Film ___ by ___." / "Complete ___ daily." Client owns a weekly theme in their own words. If client is slipping, coach creates micro-commitments. If a behavior change is noticed, coach calls it out subtly. Both sides know exactly what's expected.

buckets.label: Strong
buckets.criteria: Clear commitments but lacks specific deadlines or measurability. One side more accountable than the other. Client commitment present but vague.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Vague action steps: "Do your workouts," "Let me know how it goes." No deadline, no specific task. No verbal ownership.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No clear next steps for either party. Call ends without accountability.

positiveSignals: Client repeats back their commitment
Both sides have a named task + deadline
Coach calls out a behavior pattern change
Micro-commitment created for slipping client.
negativeSignals: Coach never follows up on previous call's commitment.
notes: "We can run into this danger zone where we're trying to care more about their journey than they do. We need to consistently revisit this — getting clients to verbally commit and take ownership." Coaches must not just tell clients what to do. Verbal commitment = ownership.
#2 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: "Most coaches say 'great, keep it up' instead of creating owned commitments on both sides."

dimensions.title: Accountability Anchor
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Is there a clear, non-negotiable accountability commitment the client owns for the week — one that is gated to a coach action (program progression, the video tool feedback)? This is best as ONE named anchor task, but a specific, verifiable, progression-gated deliverable the client confirms also qualifies — even when several items are requested — provided it's clear what the client owns and what it unlocks.

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: A clear accountability commitment the client owns and verbally confirms, gated to the coach's next action (program adjustment, the video tool feedback) — a real chain of consequence. Either form qualifies: **(a)** one explicitly-named anchor ("Send me your ___ video by Thursday — that's your accountability task this week"), **or** **(b)** a specific, verifiable deliverable the client must submit before the coach progresses ("send me these movement videos before I progress you"), even if several items are listed, as long as the deliverable and its consequence are clear and confirmed. **Time-bound** is satisfied by a hard date OR a session-relative deadline ("before our next call", "over the next two weeks before I progress you").

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Accountability gestured at but NOT clearly gated to a coach action/consequence — tasks listed with equal weight and no clear "what this unlocks", or unclear what the client actually owns. (Several tasks are fine for Strong/Elite when they are gated to progression and confirmed — see above; "multiple tasks" alone is not a downgrade.)

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No accountability anchor. Multiple vague tasks or nothing at all.

positiveSignals: Coach names "your one accountability task is..."
A specific deliverable the client confirms ("Absolutely")
The deliverable is gated to the coach's next output (progression, feedback)
A clear submission window ("before I progress you", "over the next two weeks").
negativeSignals: Vague commitments with no clear consequence
Client uncertain what they actually owe
No accountability deliverable stated before close
Tasks with no link to any coach action.
notes: The next call booking functions as a dual accountability layer. "There's that layer of accountability just by having the call in the calendar — I got to meet Dana in two weeks. I better do my stuff." The explicit weekly anchor + the booked call = dual accountability structure. Neither substitutes for the other.

"I want you to send me some videos over the next two weeks… I need to see these before I progress you," with the client confirming ("Absolutely"), is a **satisfied accountability anchor (Strong–Elite)** even though several videos are listed and the deadline is a window rather than a single date. The deliverable is specific, verifiable, owned by the client, and gated to the coach's progression decision. Do NOT cap or downgrade purely because it was framed as a set of videos or used a session-relative deadline.

dimensions.title: Struggle Handling
dimensions.whatToLookFor: When the client reveals difficulty — physical, emotional, motivational, or frustration with the program — does the coach actually coach through it, or just acknowledge it?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Coach does NOT defend, prove, or take the struggle personally. Stays grounded and fact-based. Asks questions to get to the core before offering solutions. Pre-frames if client is upset, reconnects to why, reframes ("We do not stop — we shift"), goes full circle, offers options. Client leaves feeling more capable and reconnected — not just heard.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Acknowledges struggle and offers some support. Asks some questions but doesn't fully coach through or reconnect to why. Brief or surface-level reassurance.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Struggle ignored, minimized, avoided, or coach becomes defensive. Auto-cap: 0/5, non-recoverable.

positiveSignals: Coach asks multiple questions before offering solutions
Client tone visibly shifts mid-section
Coach references original why from kickoff
Goes full circle
Offers multiple options and commits to one.
negativeSignals: "Don't worry about it, everyone goes through this"

dimensions.title: Close Quality
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the call end with emotional energy, specific celebration, and directional clarity — or just logistics?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Celebrates a specific, named progress from THIS call: "The way you pushed through ___ shows you're building ___." Reiterates direction: "This block leads directly into your ___ milestone." Warm, earned close. Client leaves energized, not just satisfied.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Positive close with some specificity but generic celebration ("You're doing great") or flat close without direction. Client leaves satisfied but not energized.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Abrupt end. Client leaves without emotional reinforcement or directional clarity.

positiveSignals: Celebration references something specific from THIS call
Direction linked to next phase
Client expresses enthusiasm or gratitude.
negativeSignals: Close rushed because booking ran late.
notes: The written breakdown in Slack/the video tool that some coaches send post-call — noted in Marcus's training as a high-motivation tool ("written breakdowns motivate") — is a post-call extension, not a substitute for the in-call close. The in-call close must still land.
#4 loss dimension per Marcus's analysis: "No emotional reinforcement at the close." Common even in strong coaches.

dimensions.title: Next Call Booking
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Is the next call booked LIVE before the call ends? Non-negotiable.

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Booked live on call (non-negotiable met). Booking link shared live. Client books during the call. Date confirmed verbally: "I see you booked for ___. We're locked in." Happens before the close.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Not booked. Call ends without next call locked in live. Automatic 0, non-recoverable.

positiveSignals: Date confirmed verbally
"We're locked in"
Booking completed before close begins.

dimensions.title: Continuity & Follow-Up Clarity
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Does the client know EXACTLY what happens after this call ends — what the coach will do, when, and how?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Coach restates the accountability anchor explicitly. States their own follow-up with specific timing: "Once you send ___, I'll the video tool you feedback by ___." Client can answer "what happens next?" without hesitation. Chain is clear: client does X by Y → coach delivers Z by W.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Follow-up mentioned but vague timing ("I'll send you feedback this week"). Anchor partially restated. Client unsure exactly what to expect or when.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: No post-call structure. Call ends with zero continuity visible.

positiveSignals: Coach gives specific day for their deliverable
Accountability anchor restated in closing
Clear cause-and-effect chain between client action and coach response.
notes: ⚠️ SCOPE NOTE — the video tool delivery: Scoring in D11 is based **only on the in-call statement** ("I'll the video tool you by ___"). Whether the coach actually sent the the video tool is post-call and **cannot be verified from the transcript**. Set `loom_delivery_verifiable: "N/A"` in output JSON. Only the presence and specificity of the in-call promise is scored.

dimensions.title: Structure & Time Management
dimensions.whatToLookFor: Did the call feel intentional and controlled — or scattered, rushed, or bloated?

buckets.label: Elite
buckets.criteria: Call flows naturally through all applicable SOP sections. Pacing smooth — not rushed, not padded. Close and booking don't feel rushed. Client never confused about where the call is going. Framework is woven in, not announced.

buckets.label: Mid
buckets.criteria: Slightly uneven pacing. Most sections covered. One section rushed or bloated, or 1 key section compressed to under 30 seconds.

buckets.label: Fail
buckets.criteria: Disorganized. Core sections missing. Flow unclear to observer and probably to client.

positiveSignals: Natural transitions between sections
Close doesn't feel rushed
No section noticeably absent.
negativeSignals: Close rushed because time ran out
Coach loses track of flow mid-call.
notes: "Don't make it robotic. You don't want to go, 'Okay, now I'm in the check-in section. Now I must move to program focus and vision.' Start to weave it into the fabric of your coaching — it'll be very natural." Robotic section announcements are a MID signal, not an ELITE signal. T.J. confirmed: the framework "shortens calls from 45–70 min to 20–26 min" without feeling scripted.

caps.condition: Next call NOT booked live during the call
caps.raw: Next call NOT booked live during the call → 0/5 on D10 (non-recoverable, confirmed by Marcus: "I don't care if you're at minute 29")

caps.condition: No connection to long-term vision at any point in the call
caps.raw: No connection to long-term vision at any point in the call → Max 10/15 on D3

caps.condition: Coach speaks >75% of the call (client passive/monologue)
caps.raw: Coach speaks >75% of the call (client passive/monologue) → Max 75 total

caps.condition: No concrete accountability commitment the client owns before close — no specific, verifiable deliverable the client confirms. A single named anchor OR a progression-gated ask ("send me your X video(s) before I progress you", client confirms) both satisfy this and do NOT trigger the cap.
caps.raw: No concrete accountability commitment the client owns before close — no specific, verifiable deliverable the client confirms. A single named anchor OR a progression-gated ask ("send me your X video(s) before I progress you", client confirms) both satisfy this and do NOT trigger the cap. → Max 10/15 on D6

caps.condition: Client struggle present but ignored or avoided
caps.raw: Client struggle present but ignored or avoided → 0/5 on D8 (non-recoverable)

caps.condition: No action steps stated for either party before close
caps.raw: No action steps stated for either party before close → Max 70 total

bands.name: ELITE
bands.description: Client feels seen, challenged, and connected to their future self. Referral and re-sign behavior expected.

bands.name: STRONG
bands.description: Good call with isolated weaknesses. Client satisfied but not deeply moved.

bands.name: INCONSISTENT
bands.description: Technically present but emotionally flat. Retention risk building quietly.

bands.name: AT RISK
bands.description: Weak client experience. Client may be doubting the process.

bands.name: FAIL
bands.description: Core elements missing. Immediate coaching intervention required.

preamble: **Scope.** Transcript only. Video delivery and in-app messaging are not part
of this. The delivery fields inside D6 and D11 are therefore N/A, and only
in-call promises are scored. Total is 100 points when D4 is active, 85 when
the call had no movement coaching and D4 is switched off.
**Discrete scoring.** Each dimension's score must be exactly one of the
bucket values listed in its table. No interpolation. Pick the bucket the call
most closely matches and let the reasoning carry the nuance.
**Why this matters.** Coaching quality drives retention directly. We cut team
churn from 5% to 2.3% in one month by improving call quality, and re-signs
show up six months after the improvement. A missed dimension today is a churn
principles: **Three-part test for every score:** depth (how far the coach went), clarity (how well it landed), and client response (did it actually land). A perfect explanation that the client didn't confirm is not elite.
**Quote-first rationale.** Every rationale must begin with a direct or paraphrased reference to a specific moment in the transcript. No impressions.
**Conservative on missing evidence.** If a behavior cannot be verified, score the lower tier of its band.

**The four client feelings are the ultimate test.** Before finalizing each score, ask: would the client leave this section feeling "this is built for me / I know exactly what to do / I trust this process / my coach is paying attention"?

**Framework use is judged by naturalness, not completeness.** A coach who covers all sections robotically scores lower on D12 than one who weaves them organically. The framework is a container, not a script.
**When D4 is disabled** the call is scored out of 85, not 100. The percentage is the raw score over 85. Report the result on the 100 scale.
